beats.say: Your fingertip is covered in tiny ridges and valleys, and your phone can read them in a blink.
Every finger has its own pattern of ridges. Even identical twins don't match.
Many phone sensors are a grid of tiny electrical pads, hidden right under the glass.
A ridge sits close to a pad, and a valley sits farther away. So each pad feels a slightly different signal.
Put all those readings together, and you get a detailed picture of your ridges.
The phone doesn't keep that picture. It picks out key points, like where a ridge ends or splits, and saves them as numbers in a secure area.
Next touch, it scans again and compares the new key points with the saved ones. Close enough, and it unlocks.
It never needs a perfect match, because no two touches are identical. Pressure and angle always change the picture a little.
That's why a wet finger can fail. Wipe it dry, and try again.
